supervisor_found_defect.found: The claim-5 suite was reported stable and was not. Supervisor measured 2 failures in 16 full-suite runs (~12%), always NEGATIVE CONTROL, always expect(results.every(r => r.code === 0)).toBe(true) — a worker subprocess exit code, not a fencing assertion.
supervisor_found_defect.root_cause: worker.ts set PRAGMA busy_timeout AFTER PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL. The WAL mode change needs a brief exclusive lock and busy_timeout was still 0, so two concurrently-opening workers collided with SQLiteError: database is locked. The throw ran at module top level, outside the .catch() attached to Effect.runPromise, so it escaped unhandled and exited non-zero.
supervisor_found_defect.why_it_was_invisible: spawnWorker captured each worker's stderr and then discarded it — never asserted, never printed. The failure carried no signal, so repeated runs read as stable. Both reviewers approved, and one re-ran the suite without recognising the race.
supervisor_found_defect.isolated_proof: Minimal two-process repro of the same pragma sequence, run outside the worktree: current order 4/40 non-zero with 'SQLiteError: database is locked'; busy_timeout first 0/40.
supervisor_found_defect.fix: busy_timeout set first; journal_mode and DDL dropped from the worker (prepareDb owns them, WAL is persistent); DB setup wrapped in try/catch with deliberate non-zero exit; every scenario now inlines captured worker stderr on failure.
supervisor_found_defect.confirmed: Supervisor re-ran the full suite 20 consecutive times after the fix: 20/20 clean. Both reviewers then re-reviewed the corrected bytes and re-ran it themselves (56 and 11 further green runs).
supervisor_found_defect.lesson: An unstable negative control is worse than an unstable test: the control's job is to show the defect returns when the fence is off, so a flaky control cannot distinguish a flake from a changed mechanism. Stability must be measured by repeated FULL-suite runs — isolated scenarios never spawn concurrently and never expose the race.

embedded.architecturalReality: Uncommenting the projector alone persists NOTHING. The commented projector at projector.ts:394 routed to run(db, event) -> SessionMessageUpdater, which treats session.next.retried as a no-op (message-updater.ts:374 -> () => Effect.void). No attempt/next_attempt_at column or retry table existed anywhere in the schema (SessionTable in session/sql.ts had no retry fields; database/schema.gen.ts had none). stability_history.defect_found_by: supervisor verification (not by the agent or the two reviewers)
stability_history.symptom: 2 failures in 16 full-suite runs (~12%), always NEGATIVE CONTROL at the `expect(results.every(r=>r.code===0)).toBe(true)` line — a worker subprocess exited non-zero. Every fencing assertion still passed, so the failure carried no fencing signal.
stability_history.root_cause: FIXTURE BUG, not a fencing bug. worker.ts set PRAGMA busy_timeout AFTER PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; the journal_mode change needs a brief exclusive lock and busy_timeout was still 0, so two workers opening the shared DB concurrently collided with SQLiteError 'database is locked'. The throw ran at module top level, OUTSIDE the Effect.runPromise .catch(), so it escaped unhandled. GREEN escaped only because its startAfterFile handshake serializes startup.
stability_history.why_it_read_as_stable: spawnWorker collected worker stderr and then discarded it; the failure was diagnostically blank.
stability_history.fix: (1) worker.ts: busy_timeout is now the first pragma; journal_mode and the DDL were dropped entirely (prepareDb in the orchestrator already creates the DB in WAL with the schema, and WAL is persistent). (2) worker.ts: DB setup is wrapped in try/catch that writes a clear stderr and exits non-zero deliberately. (3) ownership-fence.test.ts: every scenario calls assertWorkersOk, which throws with the captured worker stderr inlined on any non-zero exit. (4) re-measured: 20/20 full-suite runs green.
stability_history.lesson: a control that is itself flaky cannot distinguish a startup race from a changed mechanism — the negative control's stability is load-bearing evidence.

reviewer_deepseek.independent_runs: 11 green (5 pass / 0 fail / 22 expects each) by the reviewer; verified digests on disk; tsgo --noEmit clean.
reviewer_deepseek.mechanism_basis: claim is a single-statement onConflictDoUpdate mirroring event.ts:324-334; ISOLATION fairly isolates owner_id (winner nondeterminism asserted-away by checking one-drained-plus-one-refused only).
reviewer_deepseek.Q1_stderr_genuine: YES, with a named caveat. Child 'close' guarantees stdio drained (validated vs Node docs: 'close' fires after stdio streams closed; 'exit' may fire while streams still open), so no close-before-data race. BUT worker's process.exit(1) right after process.stderr.write can truncate pending async stderr TEXT under a pipe — exit code still non-zero so assertWorkersOk still fails the test (named), only diagnostic richness degrades. No path masks a non-zero exit as exit 0.
reviewer_deepseek.Q2_unrelated_failure: YES, three NAMED paths (none produce a false PASS): (1) GREEN handshake — if A exits non-zero before writing aReady, B polls startAfterFile forever -> Promise.all never resolves -> 30s bun:test timeout, assertWorkersOk never reached (defeats the diagnostic in exactly the A-crash case, but named as a timeout); (2) process.exit stderr truncation (see Q1); (3) s.p.7 5s deadline load-sensitivity (400ms hold vs 5s window, low probability). Also noted: test openDb connections set no busy_timeout (safe under WAL reads, latent).
reviewer_deepseek.Q3_negative_control_trustworthy: YES. Exact pre-fix config; a flake now is a worker non-zero exit surfaced by assertWorkersOk WITH stderr -> load-bearing fixture bug, not a fence signal; fresh mkdtemp per scenario -> no masking path.
reviewer_deepseek.report_only_blind_spot: statistical races below the observed run count (a ~12% flake needs ~50+ runs to bound; 31 green ~= 98%); process.exit() stderr-truncation and GREEN-handshake-timeout masking visible only on a real crash-injection or repeated loop, not in a static read of try/catch; load-sensitive timing invisible in source.
reviewer_deepseek.findings: P0 none, P1 none. P2 (non-blocking, no false PASS): GREEN handshake can mask an A-crash as a 30s timeout; process.exit(1) after stderr.write can truncate diagnostic text. P3: s.p.7 deadline load-sensitivity; manual/sample openDb no busy_timeout.

supervisor_verification_of_load_bearing_.node_close_vs_exit: VALIDATED against Node.js v26 docs (Stable API): 'close' = emitted after process ended AND stdio streams closed; 'exit' = stdio might still be open. So test:50 proc.on('close') drains stderr before Buffer.concat.
supervisor_verification_of_load_bearing_.effectflock_is_cross_process: VERIFIED on disk: tryAcquireLockDir (effect-flock.ts:176) -> atomicMkdir -> fs.makeDirectory(dir,{mode:0o700}) (line 118) on a path = lockDir + Hash.fast(sessionID) (line 257). Both workers pass the SAME lockDir + sessionID, so they race mkdir of one filesystem path -> genuine POSIX cross-process mutual exclusion, not in-process state.
supervisor_verification_of_load_bearing_.claim_atomicity: VERIFIED on disk: event_sequence.aggregate_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY (schema.ts:9) enforces single-winner; claimOrRefuse is one statement.

re_review_against_corrected_bytes.consensus: APPROVE-FOR-GATING (fencing + fixture stability). Both reviewers independently re-ran (hy3 56, deepseek 11) and verified digests on disk. Agreement on all three control questions: stderr surfacing is genuine (child 'close' drains stdio, validated vs Node docs; process.exit may truncate text but exit stays non-zero so no false PASS); surviving unrelated failures are NAMED (timeouts/assertions, not signal-less); the negative control is load-bearing (a control flake = a fixture bug, surfaced with stderr; independent tmp dirs preclude masking). No P0/P1 from either. One P2 the supervisor endorses as real-but-non-blocking: the GREEN handshake path masks the new diagnostic in exactly the A-crash-before-ready case (failure degrades to a 30s timeout instead of inlined stderr) — it does NOT produce a false PASS and is not active in the corrected fixture (A reliably writes aReady across 87+ runs), so it is recorded as a named residual risk / hardening candidate, NOT a fixture change (per task constraint: no fixture change absent a real defect; both reviewers classify it P2 non-blocking).
re_review_against_corrected_bytes.what_a_report_only_review_still_misses: the whole class of low-probability, timing-dependent, cross-process races whose failure signature is absent or masked in a single green run — exactly the class that defeated the prior approval. A soak bounds the rate but cannot prove zero; only repeated execution distinguishes 'fixed' from 'below the runs examined'.
re_review_against_corrected_bytes.residual_risk: (1) GREEN-handshake path: if A crashes before writing aReady the diagnostic degrades to a 30s timeout and assertWorkersOk's stderr is never reached — NAMED (not a false PASS), not active in the corrected fixture, a hardening candidate (ready-write deadline / poll bail-out). (2) process.exit(1) may truncate async stderr text under a pipe; exit code stays non-zero so the test still fails named. (3) A soak cannot prove a zero flake rate; 87 green runs bound the pre-fix ~12% race at ~>99.99% gone but cannot exclude a rarer residual. (4) Production wiring (fence at execution/local.ts confirmed absent at local.ts:16-29, owner release/lease-reclaim, reconcile drain-ownership vs event.ts replay-ownership) remains SLICE-012+ and out of this prototype's scope.
re_review_against_corrected_bytes.gating_decision: MAY GATE SLICE-012+. The corrected fixture removes the pre-fix defect at its root (busy_timeout first; journal_mode/DDL dropped from the worker) AND makes any future failure named (assertWorkersOk inlines stderr). Two independent fresh reviews + independent re-runs (56 + 11 + supervisor 20/20 = 87 green) converge on APPROVE-FOR-GATING with no P0/P1.
